prompt.context: Our client is a major US television network. They are trying to figure out how much to bid for the exclusive right to broadcast the 2018 Winter Olympics Games in the United States. The Winter Olympics are a huge deal and will require a significant amount of capital to secure the rights, so our client has brought us in to help them figure out the right bid amount after considering all relevant factors.
prompt.question: How much should our client bid for the exclusive US broadcasting rights to the 2018 Winter Olympics?

clarifying_info.q: Will there be subscription revenue in addition to advertising?
clarifying_info.a: No subscription revenue, but the network can keep 100% of advertising revenue.
$400K per 30-second ad for prime time (Monday-Friday 7-11 PM, and all weekend) and $200K per 30-second ad for non-prime time.

clarifying_info.q: How much advertising can be included per hour?
clarifying_info.a: Market research has shown you can include no more than 10 minutes of advertising per hour.
Yes, $1M per hour of broadcast time.

clarifying_info.q: What discount rate / time value of money should we use?
clarifying_info.a: There is a 4-year lag for receipt of revenue. Use a WACC of 10%.

exhibits.title: Winter Olympics Schedule
exhibits.shows: The broadcast schedule for the 2018 Winter Olympics, listing time slots for each phase of the event.

framework: Identify revenue streams: advertising revenue is the primary (and only) revenue source; no subscriptions
Calculate total ad revenue by time slot type: prime time vs. non-prime time, weekdays vs. weekends, plus opening/closing ceremonies
Calculate total costs: production costs + opportunity costs
Apply NPV discount for the 4-year lag to arrive at present value
Assess qualitative / intangible factors that may shift the bid above or below NPV
Provide a bid recommendation with justification

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate the total advertising revenue from broadcasting the Winter Olympics.
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment the schedule into four buckets: (1) prime-time weekdays, (2) non-prime weekdays, (3) weekends, (4) opening/closing ceremonies. Key unit conversion: 10 min ads/hr x 2 slots/min = 20 thirty-second ad slots per hour. Days 2-15 span 14 days = 10 weekdays + 4 weekend days. Opening (Day 1, Friday) and Closing (Day 16, Saturday) are each 3 hours at prime-time rates.

math.setup: Revenue = Hours x (10 ad-min/hr) x (2 slots/min) x (rate/slot). Prime rate = $400K, Non-prime rate = $200K.
steps: Prime-time weekdays (M-F 7-11pm, 10 days): 10 days x 4 hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400K = $320M
Non-prime weekdays (M-F 9am-12pm + 2-5pm = 6 hrs/day, 10 days): 10 days x 6 hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $200K = $240M
Weekend (Sat-Sun 11am-9pm = 10 hrs/day, 4 days, all prime): 4 days x 10 hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400K = $320M
Opening Ceremonies (Friday, 8-11pm = 3 hrs, prime): 1 day x 3 hrs x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400K = $24M
Closing Ceremonies (Saturday, 8-11pm = 3 hrs, prime): 1 day x 3 hrs x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400K = $24M

questions.prompt: Factoring in all costs, calculate the total profit and then the NPV of the investment.
questions.guidance: Candidate must identify three cost types: (1) production costs ($482M), (2) opportunity cost at $1M/hr for all broadcast hours, (3) time value of money via discounting at 10% WACC over 4 years. Opportunity cost hours = Opening (3 hrs) + Closing (3 hrs) + 14 broadcast days x 10 hrs/day = 6 + 140 = 146 hrs. NPV discounting: 1.10^4 = 1.4641, rounded to 1.5 for simplicity.

math.setup: Profit = Revenue - Production costs - Opportunity costs. NPV = Profit / Discount factor.
steps: Opportunity cost hours: 2 ceremony days x 3 hrs/day + 14 broadcast days x 10 hrs/day = 6 + 140 = 146 hours

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the NPV of $200M, what qualitative and intangible factors should the client consider when deciding on their final bid amount?

categories.name: Strategic / Brand Benefits
ideas: Prestige associated with hosting a major global sporting event
Opportunity to reach new viewers who may not normally watch the network
Halo effect on the network's brand and perceived quality

categories.name: Programming & Cross-Promotion
ideas: Ability to use Olympics airtime to promote other network programming
Opportunity to drive ratings for adjacent shows before and after broadcasts
Exclusive highlight clips or digital rights could extend reach

categories.name: Supplemental Revenue
ideas: Product tie-ins and sponsorship packages beyond standard ad slots

categories.name: Competitive & Game Theory Considerations
ideas: Other networks will also bid; final price is determined by competitive dynamics, not just NPV
Risk of overpaying if rival networks are willing to bid above NPV for strategic reasons
Walking away if the bid price exceeds the risk-adjusted value

categories.name: Risks & Downside
ideas: Weather, political events, or athlete scandals could depress viewership and ad revenue
Advertiser pullback if the event underperforms in ratings

recommendation: The NPV of broadcasting the 2018 Winter Olympics is $200M, which represents the quantitative floor for a bid.

Given the intangible benefits — new viewership, brand prestige, cross-promotion of other programming, and supplemental revenue opportunities — the bid should be set at approximately $200M, potentially with a modest premium to reflect strategic value.
The bid should not significantly exceed $200M without a concrete plan to monetize the intangible benefits, as there is real risk of overpaying in a competitive bidding environment.
risks: Viewership falls short of projections, reducing ad revenue below $928M
A competing network bids irrationally high, forcing a choice between overpaying or walking away
Geopolitical or athlete controversy depresses advertiser interest
next_steps: Conduct sensitivity analysis on key revenue assumptions (viewership, ad fill rates) to establish a bid range
Assess competitive intelligence on likely rival bids to refine game-theory positioning
Identify specific cross-promotional and supplemental revenue opportunities to quantify the premium above NPV
Set a firm walk-away price before entering the auction
